transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58m
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jenna Lowe (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Auricor Head of ML), Rafael Ortega (Auricor Infra), Priya Nair (CTO), Noah Lin (SRE)
Shared: benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.app/sheets/auricor-bench-0520), perf deck (link: https://redwood.app/decks/poc-auricor), tracer bundle (to follow)

Summary auto-gen (may be imperfect): Redwood p50 is substantially better than incumbent at default config; p95 shows a tail under bursty traffic likely due to batching window interplay and KV cache cold starts. SE to propose tuned knobs and run sustained load.

[00:00] Samir: All right, hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Samir from Redwood here.
[00:06] Maya: Hey Samir, thanks. We ran into a few things after your last config so we wanted to walk through numbers.
[00:12] Jenna: hi, everyone, i'll share the sheet in chat and then we'll go slide by slide, sorry my mic is a bit low.
[00:22] Rafael: got the sheet, seeing p50 numbers already. quick note, last run was 2h but we had intermittent client spikes from internal load generator.
[00:31] Samir: ok, cool. high level: p50 redwood was 32ms lower than baseline on text-gen median for our 128-token average prompt set; p95 is where we saw overlap and sometimes degraded by ~80-120ms under bursts.
[00:45] Maya: yep that's what we're seeing. the baseline (we'll call them FastServe) has a flatter p95 under high qps, curious why redwood has a tail when you do batching.
[00:58] Jenna: quick primer — our runtime uses continuous batching; batch window and max batch size together determine how requests coalesce. in steady traffic our batching reduces N by grouping tokens which lowers per-token cost and p50. but when bursts arrive the batching window can cause queues to form and then large batches at the tail which spikes generation time for those batched requests.
[01:20] Rafael: so it's the batching window ms settings? we had it at 50ms and max_batch=16.
[01:26] Jenna: right, and kv cache warmup plays a role too. some of your prompts had diverse prefixes so the kv cache had misses early in the run segments which increases step time. the combined effect is a few long outliers.
[01:40] Priya: can you explain kv cache — we're seeing reference to KV but our infra folks are not sure if that's client or server side.
[01:49] Jenna: yeah, it's server-side key-value cache for attention key/values; sometimes transcripts or tokens with long contexts mean the cache has to refill. our docs call it KV but some transcribers read it as 'kay-vee' in the sheet.
[02:00] Noah: small question — is this impacted by quantization? we ran a q4_0 variant and accuracy seemed fine but perf was different.
[02:07] Jenna: quantization reduces compute per token but it can change kernel paths; sometimes q4 runs faster per token but has slightly different memory access causing microvariance in tail. i wouldn't expect a 100ms delta solely from quant, but combined with large batches it can surface.
[02:22] Maya: ok show us the numbers — can we walk the sheet?
[02:25] Samir: yes pulling up slide 2 — here's median vs baseline, p50 redwood 88ms vs baseline 120ms. p95 chart next — see the red spikes at two time windows.
[03:00] Maya: looking at the timestamps, those spikes align with our synthetic spike windows at 12:10 and 13:04 into the run.
[03:10] Rafael: that makes sense — our client generator did a sudden 4x QPS ramp for 30s to simulate bursty traffic.
[03:16] Jenna: exact reason — during ramp we saw batches balloon to 32 because of backlog then the model had to process larger microbatches and kv misses simultaneously. our tuning knobs: reduce batching window to 20-30ms, cap max_batch to 8, enable prefix/KV prefetch for common prefixes, and enable quick-evict policy for cold shards.
[03:39] Priya: what's the tradeoff? won't reducing window increase p50?
[03:44] Jenna: slight median increase, maybe 10-15ms in our tests, but tail drops dramatically. the cost per token may go up a small percent because batching efficiency falls, but net unit-cost still favorable vs baseline in most of your traffic profiles. we'll share exact cost math.
[03:58] Samir: yep, i'll post the token-level cost sheet — it shows per-token cost with batch=8 vs batch=16 and the effective p50/p95 delta.
[04:10] Maya: another thing — we noticed during cold-starts first 5 minutes p95 is worse irrespective of batching. is that KV warmup?
[04:18] Jenna: yes warmup is key. we recommend a short ramp-up traffic or priming requests to warm the KV and model caches. also caching of top-k frequent prefixes helped in the other pilots.
[04:29] Rafael: do you have an automated priming tool?
[04:31] Jenna: we can share a small script (bash + small payload set) that replays top 200 prefixes. i'll attach as part of the tuned config.
[04:40] Noah: curious on the dedicated pool — would dedicated reduce this tail?
[04:44] Jenna: Dedicated helps by removing noisy neighbors and giving predictable device scheduling. it doesn't eliminate batching effects but reduces variance from other tenants; plus you can pin kernel choices and isolate memory pressure.
[04:56] Priya: cost question — dedicated is more costly, do you have break-even analysis vs hosted?
[05:02] Samir: yes, the cost sheet includes reserved pricing scenarios. for your projected 3M tokens/day, dedicated becomes attractive if you need consistent p95 SLAs; otherwise hosted with tuned batching is cheaper. i'll include the break-even curve.
[05:18] Maya: can we talk about p95 measurement method — are you calculating server-side only or end-to-end?
[05:23] Jenna: good call — the chart is server-side generation time; we also collected client-side RTTs in the tracer bundle. Rafael, you can see we captured client side time series as well.
[05:34] Rafael: yes logs coming, but note some of our clients had a misconfigured keepalive which added 20-40ms occasionally. that might inflate end-to-end.
[05:43] Samir: make sure to separate transport noise; we'll align on standard instrumentation for the A/B.
[05:50] Maya: what about model variants — did you test a smaller / faster variant?
[05:54] Jenna: we tested m-7b-int8 equivalent; it reduced medians by another 20-30ms but the tail behavior still followed the batching pattern. quantized variant performed similar for your metric set but we did see a 1-2% accuracy delta on a small QA prompt set — we'll run the golden prompts you shared.
[06:12] Priya: accuracy delta is a hard stop if over 1% — can you quantify?
[06:16] Jenna: initial run showed 1.4% absolute for q4_0 on our 500 sample set; we'll rerun on your 200 golden prompts and return numbers.
[06:25] Samir: action: run quantized accuracy on Auricor golden set. Jenna will own.
[06:30] Jenna: noted.
[06:33] Maya: also we hit a surprising regression in one run where p95 jumped by 220ms only on a single host — seems like a scheduling jitter.
[06:40] Jenna: if you can share the tracer for that host we'll dig; scheduling jitter sometimes due to GC or background snapshotting on the instance. Dedicated mitigates but we also have knob to aggressively isolate CC threads.
[06:52] Rafael: will collect that tracer.
[07:00] [07:00-25:00 omitted brief walkthrough of spreadsheet rows and charts — conversation includes numbers and quick tradeoffs, some cross talk]
[25:30] Samir: ok jumping to the long-run test plan — propose: 2-hour sustained 1k RPS with 30s synthetic bursts every 10min, collect both client and server traces, run with batch window 50/30 configs, and run baseline provider in parallel.
[25:47] Priya: timeline?
[25:49] Samir: earliest Wed 05/27, need your infra to open temporary test endpoints and seed traffic.
[25:55] Rafael: that's doable, we'll confirm.
[26:02] Maya: can Redwood instrument token-level cost in the run output? we need per-run cost estimate for exec team.
[26:09] Samir: yes, we'll include token counts and compute seconds per run to estimate cost; Jenna will also include batch-distribution histogram.
[26:18] Jenna: one more note — routing we discussed earlier: we can route by latency SLO and have an automatic fallback to a cheaper model during overloads. that reduces p95 impact at cost of sometimes returning a shorter/higher-compression response.
[26:34] Maya: is that safe for our use case? we have regulatory constraints — can't send certain PHI to non-private endpoints.
[26:41] Samir: good flag — we can restrict fallback to model variants within the same privacy boundary. for your Private deployment we can enforce no-fallback to hosted. we'll document policy.
[26:54] Priya: onboarding for Private — what's the rough lead time? network, KMS setup, compliance review?
[27:00] Jenna: typical private deployment is 4-8 weeks depending on KMS and networking approvals. we've done fast tracks in 3 weeks with pre-approved templates.
[27:10] Samir: we'll start by sending the Private deployment checklist; Priya please share SOC2 contact.
[27:16] Priya: will do.
[27:20] Maya: any other blockers?
[27:23] Noah: small item — our observability team wants token-level logging suppressed except for aggregate metrics; can Redwood filter?
[27:30] Jenna: yes we support redaction and token scrubbing; we can offer aggregate token metrics and never store raw user text for hosted plans unless explicitly enabled. for Private you control retention.
[27:46] Samir: ok moving toward decisions — immediate focus is eliminating the tail for high-QPS bursts. proposal: 1) run long test with current settings, 2) run with tuned settings (batch_window=25ms, max_batch=8, kv_prefetch), 3) run quantized variant on golden prompts, 4) A/B vs baseline.
[28:08] Rafael: and we'll provide tracer logs and confirm test infra.
[28:12] Maya: what's acceptable p95 for us to move to dedicated? we need a number.
[28:16] Priya: for product launch we want p95 < 350ms end-to-end for 95% of windows.
[28:22] Samir: got it — we'll target server-side p95 < 250ms to allow transport noise buffer.
[28:29] Jenna: i'll craft a run config and a short primer doc for your infra team.
[28:33] Samir: anything else?
[28:36] Maya: one more — can you add the cost sensitivity if we cap batch to 8 for 24/7 ops? we need a 90-day burn projection.
[28:45] Samir: yes i'll include a 90-day projection in the spreadsheet.
[28:50] Priya: ok thanks.
[28:53] [28:53-47:00 continued deep technical Q&A — notes omitted to keep transcript focused on actionables; included in full recording]
[47:05] Jenna: quick callout from the lab — when we simulated clients with different sequence length distribution (some 512 token conversations), the p95 worsened more; your production distribution matters more than median.
[47:18] Rafael: we can share production seq len distribution.
[47:22] Samir: please do. that will change batch-expectation math.
[47:28] Maya: ok wrapping up — can you list owners and dates?
[47:32] Samir: yeah quick recap:
- Samir: share cost sheet and break-even (due 2026-05-24)
- Jenna: tuned config + priming script + batch histograms (due 2026-05-23)
- Rafael (Auricor): tracer logs and endpoint setup for long test (due 2026-05-25)
- Jenna: quantized accuracy run on 200 golden prompts (due 2026-05-26)
- Priya: share compliance contact and confirm Private interest (due 2026-05-28)

[48:10] Priya: sounds good. one last ask — can you upload the perf deck to our shared folder?
[48:15] Samir: done, uploaded to your folder and pinned in the thread.
[48:20] Maya: thanks everyone.
[48:23] Samir: thank you all. we'll follow up via the Slack thread and a calendar invite for the long-run test.
[48:30] [call ends]

Notes about transcription: occasional mishears ("kay-vee" for KV, "fast serve" for FastServe); speaker labels are accurate to the best of auto-transcribe but a couple of lines attributed to Samir may be Jenna. Full recording in CRM.
